name: radio-group
purpose: RadioGroup is the one "pick one of a few" component: it picks exactly one value from a short list of labelled options shown at once. The root is a `radiogroup` that owns the value (`v-model`), the shared form `name`, the group `disabled` / `required` / `invalid` state, the layout axis and the option look (`variant`), and hands them to every `RadioGroup.Item` through `provide`/`inject`; each item draws a radio circle beside its label, or, with `variant="card"`, a bordered card with an optional icon, description and trailing tag (Radix and shadcn style card radios the same way). The options are composed as `RadioGroup.Item`s, or passed as data through `options`. Because the items are native radios that share one `name`, the group is a single tab stop and the arrow keys move the selection, as the APG radio group pattern asks, with no wiring by the consumer. Before 6.0 the bare circle was `RadioButton` and the card look was `RadioCards`; both are folded in here.
useWhen: Use RadioGroup to pick exactly one of two to seven options shown at once in a form; set `variant="card"` when each option needs an icon, a description or card weight (plans, roles). For more options use Select; to switch a view or mode in place use ToggleGroup; for the theme in app chrome use ThemeSwitcher.
A required choice of one option among two to seven, where every option should stay visible (billing cycle, region, notification channel).
A settings form that posts with a native `form` or `FormData`: the selected value submits under `name`.
A choice inside a `Field` that needs the group label, description and error wired to it.
avoidWhen: More than about seven options, or options loaded on demand → use `Select`.
A single on/off setting → use `Switch` or `Checkbox`.
Several options that may all be on at once → use `Checkbox` items in a `Field.Set`.
A compact segmented control that switches a view → use `ToggleGroup`.
related: toggle-group` — a segmented button group for switching views or filters.
theme-switcher` — the system / light / dark choice in app chrome.
select` — one value from a longer list.
field` — wraps the group with its title, description and error; `Field.Set` with `Field.Legend` names it natively.
bestPractices: Name the group: put it in a `Field.Set` with a `Field.Legend`, give the `Field` a `Field.Title`, or set `aria-label` on the root.
Keep labels short and parallel, and order options by likelihood or by a natural sequence.
Preselect a sensible option when one exists; leave it empty only when the person must choose deliberately, and then set `required`.
Use `orientation="horizontal"` only for two or three short options; longer lists read better stacked.
Set `name` whenever the form posts natively; without it the radios share a generated name that is still submitted.
Do not compose radios by hand (a `Field.Label` choice card around a bare radio): every radio is a `RadioGroup.Item` inside a `RadioGroup`.

With `variant="card"`, give options a `description` rather than a longer label, and use the `tag` slot for a price or a "Recommended" tag. Use `orientation="horizontal"` for cards that share a row; they wrap at 12rem.
Pass `options` when the list is data (a plan catalog, roles from an API); the `option` slot replaces an option's label, for a custom body such as an avatar.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name shared by every radio; the selected value submits under it. Empty uses a generated name so the radios still group.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Layout axis: options stacked, or in a wrapping row. Arrow keys move the selection on both axes either way.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Look of every option: a circle beside its label, or a bordered card for options with an icon, a description or card weight (plans, roles). `RadioGroupVariant`, exported.

props.name: options
props.doc: Options rendered as `RadioGroup.Item` rows, in place of composed items (`TOption extends RadioGroupOption`: `{ value, label, description?, icon?, ariaLabel?, disabled? }`, exported); extra fields reach the `option` and `tag` slots. Empty renders the default slot.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every option and applies the disabled tokens.

props.name: required
props.doc: Requires a selection: sets `aria-required` on the group and `required` on the radios, so a native form blocks an empty submit.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the group invalid: sets `aria-invalid` on the group and on every radio.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The `RadioGroup.Item`s. Not rendered while `options` is set.

slots.name: option
slots.notes: Body of one data-driven option, in place of its label.

slots.name: tag
slots.notes: Trailing content of one data-driven option, such as a price or a tag.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import RadioGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const cycle = ref('monthly')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioGroup
    v-model="cycle"
    name="billing-cycle"
    aria-label="Billing cycle"
  >
    <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="yearly">Yearly, two months free</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item
      value="contract"
      disabled
    >
      Annual contract
    </RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
</template>

examples.name: Horizontal
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import RadioGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const protocol = ref('https')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioGroup
    v-model="protocol"
    name="protocol"
    orientation="horizontal"
    aria-label="Protocol"
  >
    <RadioGroup.Item value="http">HTTP</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="https">HTTPS</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="both">Both</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
</template>

examples.name: Disabled
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import RadioGroup from '@aziontech/webkit/radio-group'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const plan = ref('pro')
</script>

<template>
  <RadioGroup
    v-model="plan"
    name="plan"
    disabled
    aria-label="Plan"
  >
    <RadioGroup.Item value="free">Free</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="pro">Pro</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="enterprise">Enterprise</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
</template>
